title: P300 dataset from Hoffmann et al 2008
description: EEG recordings from eight subjects (four with disabilities, four able-bodied) performing a P300-based brain-computer interface task. Subjects silently counted flashes of a prescribed target image among six household-object images (television, telephone, lamp, door, window, radio) flashed in random sequences. Each subject completed four sessions of six runs, recorded with 32 EEG channels at 2048 Hz, supporting evaluation of P300 classification for environment control.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Biosemi ActiveTwo system (32 electrodes, 2048 Hz, standard 10-20 montage). Six images were flashed for 100 ms with a 400 ms inter-stimulus interval. Subjects counted target flashes silently, with no feedback (offline). Each subject completed 4 sessions of 6 runs. Original analysis used BLDA and FLDA classifiers with leave-one-session-out cross-validation.
